title: Root account has MFA enabled
remediation: Sign in to the AWS Management Console as the root user, navigate to IAM > Security credentials, and assign a virtual or hardware MFA device to the root account immediately.
rationale: The root account has unrestricted administrative power across the entire AWS account. Without MFA, credentials compromise results in complete account takeover.

title: No root account active access keys
remediation: Sign in as the root user, open IAM > Security credentials, and delete any active access keys. Use IAM Identity Center or dedicated IAM roles for programmatic access instead.
rationale: Root access keys cannot be constrained by permission boundaries or SCPs, presenting an extreme risk if leaked or committed to version control.

title: All console users have MFA enabled
remediation: Enforce multi-factor authentication for all IAM users with console access passwords. Apply an IAM policy requiring MFA for API and console actions.
rationale: Passwords alone are vulnerable to credential stuffing, phishing, and spray attacks. MFA adds essential second-factor defense.

title: Strong account password policy enforced
remediation: Navigate to IAM > Account settings and enforce: minimum length of 14+ characters, require uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols, prevent password reuse (24), and expire in 90 days.
rationale: Weak passwords facilitate brute-force attacks and lateral movement within the cloud environment.

title: IAM access keys rotated within 90 days
remediation: Create a new key pair for users with keys older than 90 days, update client applications, deactivate the old key, verify functionality, and delete the legacy key.
rationale: Regular rotation reduces the window of vulnerability if credentials are unintentionally exposed.

title: No unused IAM credentials over 90 days
remediation: Review dormant IAM users and credentials unused for 90+ days. Deactivate or delete stale access keys and remove console access passwords.
rationale: Dormant credentials increase the attack surface and represent unmonitored persistence pathways.

title: No wildcard admin policies attached
remediation: Replace policies with Action: '*' and Resource: '*' with least-privilege scoped permissions tailored to specific service and resource requirements.
rationale: Overly permissive admin rights violate the principle of least privilege and amplify blast radius.

title: Policies attached to groups or roles rather than individual users
remediation: Detach inline and managed policies from individual users. Create functional IAM groups or roles and attach policies at the group/role level.
rationale: Direct user attachments lead to permission sprawl, inconsistency, and difficult compliance auditing.

title: S3 Block Public Access enabled at bucket and account level
remediation: Enable all 4 Block Public Access settings (BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets) at both account and bucket level.
rationale: Public exposure of S3 storage is one of the leading root causes of enterprise data breaches.

title: No public S3 ACLs or public bucket policies
remediation: Remove all ACL grants to 'AuthenticatedUsers' and 'AllUsers'. Revoke public Principal: '*' clauses from bucket policies unless intentionally hosting public static assets.
rationale: Public bucket access allows unauthenticated external actors to read, exfiltrate, or tamper with data.

title: S3 default encryption enabled (SSE-KMS or SSE-S3)
remediation: Enable default encryption on the S3 bucket using AWS KMS (SSE-KMS) or Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3).
rationale: Encryption at rest ensures confidentiality and satisfies regulatory compliance standards.

title: S3 bucket versioning enabled
remediation: Enable versioning on the S3 bucket via S3 Console > Bucket Properties > Bucket Versioning.
rationale: Versioning protects against accidental deletion, ransomware, and unauthorized data modification.

title: S3 server access logging enabled
remediation: Enable Server Access Logging on the bucket, directing logs to a dedicated, secured log bucket.
rationale: Access logs provide audit trails required for incident investigation and forensic compliance.

title: S3 bucket enforces TLS in transit (SecureTransport)
remediation: Add a bucket policy denying s3:* actions when 'aws:SecureTransport' condition is false.
rationale: Enforcing TLS protects data confidentiality and prevents eavesdropping or man-in-the-middle attacks.

title: Security groups do not allow unrestricted SSH (22) or RDP (3389)
remediation: Modify security group rules to restrict ports 22 and 3389 to specific trusted corporate IP CIDRs or migrate management access to AWS Systems Manager Session Manager.
rationale: Unrestricted administrative ports on the internet are constant targets for automated brute force and exploit attempts.

title: Security groups do not allow unrestricted all-port ingress
remediation: Remove security group ingress rules allowing all traffic (-1 protocol or port 0-65535) from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.
rationale: Opening all ports to the internet exposes internal services, databases, and debugging ports indiscriminately.

title: EBS default encryption enabled for account in region
remediation: Enable EBS default encryption in the EC2 Console > EC2 Dashboard > Settings > EBS encryption.
rationale: EBS default encryption ensures all newly provisioned EBS volumes and snapshots are encrypted at rest.

title: All attached and unattached EBS volumes are encrypted
remediation: Create snapshots of unencrypted EBS volumes, copy the snapshots with encryption enabled, and create new encrypted volumes to replace unencrypted volumes.
rationale: Unencrypted volumes risk data exposure if underlying storage hardware is compromised or misplaced.

title: VPC Flow Logs enabled for all VPCs
remediation: Create Flow Logs for all VPCs sending accepted and rejected IP traffic telemetry to CloudWatch Logs or S3.
rationale: Flow logs provide visibility into network anomalies, communication patterns, and potential breach activity.

title: CloudTrail multi-region trail enabled and logging
remediation: Configure at least one multi-region CloudTrail trail logging management events with logging status active.
rationale: Without comprehensive CloudTrail logging, administrative actions and potential attacks cannot be audited.

title: CloudTrail log file validation enabled
remediation: Enable log file validation on all trails to cryptographically verify log file integrity.
rationale: Log validation uses digest files and digital signatures to ensure audit trails have not been modified or deleted.

title: AWS Config configuration recorder enabled
remediation: Enable AWS Config recorder and delivery channel in each active region to record resource configurations.
rationale: AWS Config tracks historical resource configurations and configuration drift for compliance validation.

title: Amazon GuardDuty detector enabled
remediation: Enable GuardDuty across all active regions to leverage machine learning threat detection on CloudTrail, VPC, and DNS logs.
rationale: GuardDuty provides continuous intelligent threat detection to identify compromised credentials and anomalous behaviors.

title: Customer managed KMS keys have annual rotation enabled
remediation: Enable automatic key rotation for all active customer-managed symmetric KMS keys in KMS Console or via CLI.
rationale: Annual cryptographic key rotation limits the volume of ciphertext encrypted under a single key version.

title: RDS database instances have storage encryption enabled
remediation: Enable KMS encryption for all RDS databases. Note that unencrypted instances must be migrated via snapshot copy.
rationale: Database storage encryption ensures data, automated backups, and read replicas are protected at rest.

title: RDS instances are not publicly accessible
remediation: Modify RDS instances to set 'PubliclyAccessible' to false and place databases inside private VPC subnets.
rationale: Databases exposed directly to the public internet invite continuous brute-force attacks and injection attempts.

title: RDS automated backup retention period is at least 7 days
remediation: Modify RDS instance backup configuration to set backup retention period between 7 and 35 days.
rationale: Inadequate backup retention hampers disaster recovery and business continuity objectives.

title: RDS production instances configured with Multi-AZ deployment
remediation: Enable Multi-AZ deployment for production RDS databases to maintain synchronous standby replicas across availability zones.
rationale: Single-AZ deployments fail to meet high availability and business continuity requirements during infrastructure failures.
